POINT-IN-TIME RESEARCH

The historical laboratory.

Freeze a thesis before revealing subsequent outcomes. Separate a model's economic consistency from a stock's price performance.

Retrospective exercise: the analyst may already know the outcome. Date filtering controls the modeled information set; it cannot remove hindsight or selection bias. Browser-local locks are not tamper-proof, and source files can be inspected. This is not evidence of predictive alpha.

01 · Choose the information set

Select a company in the workbench, then choose a date. Only filings available by that date can enter the experiment.

Same-day filings are conservatively available the next trading session where supplied by the source ledger. Fiscal year labels are not calendar years.

02 · Freeze, then evaluate

Your current workbench assumptions and business story are copied into a new immutable local record.

Start with the mature-company baseline

Microsoft FY2019 is a separate, dated operating-company case before the harder NVIDIA examples. Use the original filing and contemporaneous outlook, then freeze the assumptions before opening later outcomes.

One baseline plus four NVIDIA vintages are five retrospective case studies, not a broad strategy backtest or a clean blind holdout.

NVIDIA · 2021–2024 research protocol

Use the annual as-filed snapshots when available, with the exact fiscal period and availability date. GPU demand, gaming, data centers and the AI transition require distinct narratives at each date.

01

Reconstruct the story

Identify segment growth, customer concentration, supply constraints and competitive threats in filings available then. Do not import later AI outcomes into an earlier base case.

02

Fund the growth

Translate the story into revenue, operating margins, taxes and sales-to-capital. Test chip-cycle normalization and explain the duration of excess returns.

03

Reconcile the shares

Use a dated share count. Adjust both valuation per share and historical prices for subsequent splits before comparing levels. Price returns alone do not measure valuation error.

A handful of annual cases is a case study, not a statistically validated backtest. Use a predeclared universe including failures, rolling out-of-sample windows, transaction costs and a benchmark for strategy evaluation.

What would the quoted price require?

Reverse DCF is a conditional diagnostic after the original assumptions are frozen. Multiple different economic stories can reproduce the same quote.

03 · Diagnose the forecast, then revise

Reveal later filings only after locking. Compare operating outcomes separately from market prices. A large miss is a prompt to investigate, not proof of a broken valuation identity.

The original frozen record remains unchanged. Revisions are explicitly hindsight-informed and must be tested on a new holdout period.

Five dated teaching cases

Microsoft FY2019 is the ordinary-business comparator; NVIDIA FY2021–FY2024 are four selected GPU-cycle cases. These are retrospective case studies, not a systematic backtest, representative sample or evidence of trading alpha.

THE COMPREHENSION AUDIT

Can you explain
what creates value?

Work the mechanism before checking the answer. These original exercises test transfer, not memorization.

Worked example · Growth can destroy value

Hold next year's NOPAT fixed at 100. Let WACC = 10% and marginal ROIC = 5%.

2% stable growth

750.00

Reinvestment = 100 × 2% / 5% = 40
Value = (100 − 40) / (10% − 2%)

4% stable growth

333.33

Reinvestment = 100 × 4% / 5% = 80
Value = (100 − 80) / (10% − 4%)

The economic lesson

Growth ≠ value

Growth funded at returns below the cost of capital destroys value. The ability to stop bad investment may add control value.

Executable model checks

These checks test identities and implementation consistency. Passing them does not establish forecast accuracy or investment performance.

EVIDENCE BEFORE PRECISION

Know what is
inside the model.

Import a company

JSON snapshot or CSV with one header row and one data row. Amounts and shares must both be in millions. Nothing is uploaded to a server.

Model boundaries

  • Ordinary nonfinancial companies. Financials require equity/regulatory-capital models. Cyclicals need normalized drivers; the generic fade is not a cycle model.
  • Unlevered FCFF / nominal WACC. Default constant WACC, or cumulative annual rates in a dated research path; simple cash taxes; no NOL ledger, currency conversion, distress or financing path.
  • Reinvestment. Positive incremental revenue ÷ sales-to-capital. Decline does not automatically release capital; separate maintenance needs are not modeled. Terminal reinvestment = NOPAT × g / ROIC. No unfunded terminal growth.
  • Accounting judgment. R&D, leases, stock compensation and acquisition-related adjustments must be made coherently before import. Reported data are not automatically economic data.
  • Per-share convention. Period-end shares preferred. Weighted-average diluted shares are a disclosed approximation; options are not separately valued by the model.
  • Local persistence. Saved cases stay in this browser's local storage. Unsaved imports remain in this tab only. Export JSON to keep or transfer them.
